Guide · churches · PTZ cameras · 6 picks

The best PTZ camera for your church. Start from the distance.

The camera that suits a church is the one that frames the pastor from where it has to sit. This guide ranks six PTZ cameras on i9Store by how far they reach, what they plug into and what they cost, and says what each one is not for.

Prices listed USD, before taxAvailability read 25 Nov 2026By i9StoreUpdated 26 Nov 2026

How we chose

Three questions, in this order.

1. Does it reach the pulpit? Measure from where the camera can be mounted to where the pastor stands. A camera’s zoom sets the farthest distance at which it still frames a head-and-shoulders close-up; past it, full zoom gives a medium close-up or a medium shot. Each pick shows that distance, worked out from the maker’s published angles with the same maths as i9’s room planner.

2. Does it plug into your switcher? HDMI suits a small switcher close by, SDI suits long cable runs, NDI suits a network. Power over Ethernet saves a power outlet at the camera, if your switch has the right class of port.

3. What does it cost, and can you get it? Listed prices and the availability the store showed on 25 Nov 2026. Not on the list: PTZOptics and BirdDog, which many church guides recommend, because i9Store doesn’t sell them.

One joystick for all of them

Two cameras and up: add a controller.

With two or more PTZ cameras, a joystick controller recalls presets (“pulpit”, “worship”, “baptism”) on any camera with one button. Stay with one brand: the store’s controllers are made for their own cameras.

The one-operator setup skips the controller and uses the cameras’ own presets; the three-camera setup adds the Panasonic AW-RP60.

Church PTZ questions.

Zoom, outputs, 4K and how many cameras.

What zoom does a church PTZ camera need?

Enough for the distance from the camera to the pulpit. For a head-and-shoulders close-up, a 12× camera works to about 19 ft, a 20× camera to about 31 ft and a 24× camera to about 34 ft. Farther than that, full zoom gives a medium close-up or a medium shot.

NDI, SDI or HDMI for a church?

HDMI is fine for short runs into a small switcher like the ATEM Mini. SDI carries video over long coax runs with locking connectors. NDI sends video, control and, with PoE, power over one network cable to an NDI switcher or software.

Do I need 4K?

Most church streams go out in HD. 4K helps if you record for later editing or crop in post, or feed a large LED wall. All six cameras here shoot 4K; the CR-N500, the UE80 and the Tail 2 reach 60p.

How many PTZ cameras does a church need?

Two cover most services: one wide, one following the speaker. A third on the worship team helps larger rooms. One joystick controller recalls presets on all of them.

Why isn’t PTZOptics or BirdDog on this list?

i9Store doesn’t sell them, so they are not ranked here. Every camera on this page is a live i9Store listing.
